about.title: Angels Camp Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Angels Camp draws steady foot traffic through its historic downtown along S Main Street and Rt 49, where sidewalks, shop entrances, and parking areas see visitors year-round. When a property owner lets a hazard go unfixed — a wet floor, broken stair, uneven pavement, or poor lighting — the result can be a serious fall injury. California law asks whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and failed to correct it or warn visitors. That's why what happens right after a fall matters: photos of the hazard, names of witnesses, and any nearby surveillance footage can all shape whether a claim holds up. Our team handles premises liability claims in Angels Camp and can review the facts, explain your options, and work on a contingency basis so you owe nothing unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Choose Us for Your Fall Claim in Angels Camp

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Timely Evidence
items.desc: Because California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard, we can help gather maintenance records, incident reports, and photos before they disappear.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks, so we can send a preservation request quickly to protect evidence that shows how long a hazard existed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're partly at fault for not noticing a hazard, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery reduced by your share of responsibility, so it's worth having your case evaluated.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Angels Camp?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, though claims against a public entity (like a city-owned sidewalk) usually require a much shorter notice period. We can confirm which deadline applies based on where the fall happened.

items.question: What if I fell at a downtown shop near S Main Street and no one saw it happen?
items.answer: Even without witnesses, evidence like photos of the hazard, your shoes and clothing, and any nearby security cameras can help establish what happened. We can also request that the business preserve footage before it's automatically deleted.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to us about my case?
items.answer: No, there's no obligation to move forward. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
